newsitem.title: NORWAY: Former Norwegian premier wants to be WHO boss.
newsitem.headline: Former Norwegian premier wants to be WHO boss.

text.p: Former Norwegian prime minister Gro Harlem Brundtland indicated on Sunday she was prepared to seek the top job at the World Health Organisation (WHO).
Brundtland, 57, a medical doctor by training, resigned as prime minister last October after dominating Norwegian politics for more than a decade.
She subsequently declared that she would also leave parliament this year, leading to speculation that she was aspiring for a post at a United Nations body such as the WHO.

"You feel an obligation to make a contribution if you are well and capable of doing it," Brundtland told Norwegian television. "It means something to me if many people believe this would be a job where I simply can make a contribution."

Foreign Ministry spokesman Geir Pedersen said earlier that she had received requests from several WHO members to give a positive signal to the agency's board and had now delivered her intention before a May deadline.
Brundtland has enjoyed international recognition since 1983 as chairwoman of the U.N. World Commission on Environment and Development and is also known as a champion of women's issues.
The national NTB news agency said Britain and the United States were among those who had asked her to stand as a candidate for the position of WHO director-general.

The three-time premier had long been mooted as a favourite to head the Geneva-based agency although she herself had always refused to comment on speculation that she might leave Norway for an international position.
Brundtland told NTB she had decided she would only be available for the top WHO job if other countries wanted her and she was not yet a formal candidate.
"Nobody is a candidate so far. It will be possible to nominate candidates to the job as director-general from the summer of 1997," she was quoted as saying.

The WHO, which has come under increasing criticism for mismanagement, is expected to announce in May 1998 who will take over as director general from incumbent Hiroshi Nakajima of Japan two months later.
